extracted.intended_audience: comedians and performers (solo artists, improv teams, clowns, sketch writers/performers) interested in submitting to The Peoples Improv Theater festivals (NYC)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and submission criteria for multiple Peoples Improv Theater festivals (SoloComNYC, March Madness, Clown Days, INDIE-pendence, NYC Sketchfest), describing eligibility, material requirements, format expectations, scheduling, and fee policy. Intended to help performers decide suitability and prepare submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SoloComNYC new-material requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All shows presented are 75% – 100% new material, and are created specifically for the festival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SoloComNYC is a festival of new solo work; the festival has launched many new solo comedies that went on to longer runs. The festival's goal is to push artists to create a show that is meaningful, personal and to follow the fear. Programming includes Mainstage and Additional programming slots across specific times (e.g., Mainstage shows at 5:30, 7, 8, & 9:15; other days listed with specific time slots) — submit with the expectation your material must fit festival scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: SoloComNYC artistic intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows should be meaningful, personal, and demonstrate risk-taking ('follow the fear').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SoloCom emphasizes new, personally-driven material created specifically for the festival; applicants should highlight the personal/meaningful angle and intentions to present new, risky work.

rubrics_metrics.name: March Madness format and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: March Madness Improv Tournament is a knockout-style improv competition where teams go head-to-head in various games and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a bracket-style, competitive format hosted Fridays and Saturdays; teams should be prepared for competitive games and successive elimination rounds. Hosted by improv duo NANA; attend/participate in Friday and Saturday night shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clown Days fee policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clown Days is a two-day celebration of clowning; applicants will not be charged to submit or participate. Emphasize that there are no financial barriers to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clown Days performance-format eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Looking for clowns with a shorter act that could be part of a larger hour-long block, and hour-long clown shows that could have their own block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should indicate whether their piece is a short act appropriate for inclusion in a larger hour-long block or a standalone hour-long show. The festival programs both short-block acts and full-length clown shows across the two festival days (dates: Sunday June 28th and Monday June 29th).

rubrics_metrics.name: INDIE-pendence Fest eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A celebration of independent improv teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus is on independent improv teams; further submission details and selection criteria pending (stay tuned for IndieFest’26 information). Teams should be independent rather than institutionally affiliated or part of PIT house teams (implied).

rubrics_metrics.name: NYC Sketchfest focus
rubrics_metrics.description: A 4-day festival dedicated to sketch comedy performance and writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch performers and sketch writers should prepare material suitable for a multi-day festival; annual festival programming and submission details to be announced (reference to 11th annual NYC Sketchfest and upcoming announcements for SketchFest ’26).

rubrics_metrics.name: General submission accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Click here to submit for FREE (general submissions link presented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site advertises free submission access (explicit for Clown Days and at the top of the festivals page). Applicants should use the provided submission link and expect that at least some festivals hosted by PIT accept free submissions; verify festival-specific instructions once submission pages are reached.
